questions: Did the party hire Drop Dead Ned for 100 gold and bring him to Brandon's Barrow?
Does Drop Dead Ned refund 10 gold to the party whenever they permit him to murder someone and do whatever he wishes with the body?
Did disturbed earth at the entrance to Brandon's Barrow indicate that the door had been opened recently?
Did the antechamber contain three gem-inlaid mosaics and passages leading east and west?
Did one of the antechamber's mosaics depict Sir Brandon killing a dragon by driving his sword through the roof of its mouth?
Did the mosaics depict Sir Brandon gathering his companions, including Alfred portrayed as a shaggy giant wielding a greatsword?
Did the eastern passage lead to a crypt where four poorly equipped goblins were arguing about politics and whether a speaking stick was necessary?
Did Sir Phidipaldi, in full plate, enter the goblins' midst, take their speaking stick, and compel them to sit and speak only with his permission?
Did Snurk the Walkout introduce the group as the Free Goblin Society, naming Grimble Who Holds the Stick, Watok the Scribbler, and Peg Who Had the Torch as its members?
Did Snurk the Walkout declare that the Free Goblin Society intended to claim Brandon's Barrow as a collective free of King Hogboon?
Did Sir Phidipaldi tell the goblins that he was Sir Brandon's son and that he had no claim to the barrow itself?
Did Sir Phidipaldi ask the goblins to help him recover his father's bequeathed possessions?
Did Sir Phidipaldi offer to clear the barrow's evil, conceal the goblins from King Hogboon, and leave them the barrow in exchange for their help and permission to take Sir Brandon's goods?
Did the Free Goblin Society accept Sir Phidipaldi's arrangement and agree that the party could take anything because none of the goblins believed in property?
Did the goblin crypt contain a sealed alcove behind a heavy flagstone?
Did the goblin crypt contain an alcove holding an ornate jewel-encrusted ceremonial dagger?
Did Peg Who Had the Torch tell the party that the goblins had sealed a gray ooze behind the flagstone because they did not want it in their home but believed they had no right to kill it?
Did the freed gray ooze, once unsealed, advance to attack the party?
Did Squints kill the gray ooze with a precisely slung stone?
Did Trout commend Squints for killing the ooze?
Was the Free Goblin Society initially condemn the party for killing the gray ooze, viewing it as judging another life?
Did Waymon Tisdale tell the goblins that they had sealed the ooze away to starve and had effectively forced it to attack because it could not be reasoned with?
Did the Free Goblin Society concede that Waymon was wise and admit that they had outsourced violence to feel safe?
Was it established that the ceremonial dagger dated from when the barrow was created and sealed, and would likely sell for more than 200 gold in a major city?

Did the Free Goblin Society tell the party that more than four goblins had entered the barrow, but several had been killed below by a figure from the mosaics—a very large being armed with a huge sword?
Did Dr Uriah discover a secret door in the eastern wall of the goblin room?
Did the secret door in the goblin room lead to a chamber containing an ornate dark-wood chest and seven unlit white candles in golden holders worth 50 gold each?
Was there a chest that contained a quarterstaff and monastic robes that Brother Dirk identified as relics of Saint Arthur?
Did Brother Dirk call Saint Arthur's robes sacred treasures too holy to wear and object to any threat of burning them?
Did Dr Uriah determine that the robes were not cursed, put them on despite Brother Dirk's objection, and take the quarterstaff?
Did the western statue chamber hold four eight-foot stone knights labeled Valor (a giant with sword and shield), Piety (a praying staff-bearer), Wisdom (a reader), and Duty (a burdened figure)?
Did a dripping sound from the statue room lead northwest into a ruined chapel containing a mold-covered statue of Saint Arthur, the bearded patron of hunters, holding a spear?
Did Sir Phidipaldi's attempt to clear the mold from Saint Arthur's statue trigger a poisoned spore cloud that he resisted without taking harm?
Did Sir Phidipaldi receive Saint Arthur's blessing after cleaning his statue?
Did the party find three goblins dismembered by sword blows at the foot of the stairs in a mosaic-covered corridor, apparently killed by sword strikes while fleeing back toward the stairs?
Did the party hear scratching sounds coming from farther west in the mosaic corridor?
Did the party discover a circular pool in a southern side chamber containing living green slimes floating above a submerged human skeleton?
Did the party use their powers to talk to a slime in the pool room?
Did a green slime tell the party that a half-dead, furious giant roams the barrow below and had killed the goblins?
Did a green slime give the party permission to take the treasure from its pool?
Was the slime pool's treasure a human skeleton with gold teeth worth 20 gold and a silver dagger?
Did Waymon Tisdale discover an incongruous groove in the pool chamber's southern wall that led to a hidden passage?
Did the hidden door open into a chamber containing a stylized statue of a noblewoman holding a stone sword horizontally toward a pair of closed stone doors?
Did a female voice enter the party's minds in the chamber with the woman statue asking, "What makes a true knight?"
Did the party answer the voice's question in the chamber with the woman statue by naming the four virtues—valor, duty, wisdom, and piety—causing the southern stone doors to open?
Did the party enter a burial chamber dominated by a wooden dragon-headed ship holding a stone sarcophagus of a sleeping knight, surrounded by five urns, a kite shield, and a jeweled chalice?
Was the sarcophagus engraved with Brandon's name, confirming it as Sir Brandon's tomb?
Did Brother Dirk kneel and pray at Sir Brandon's tomb?
Did Trout take the jeweled chalice worth 600 gold despite Brother Dirk's hope that it would be given to the church?
Did Sir Brandon's skeleton, still wearing plate armor, hold a magical, uncursed sword etched "All shadows yield to my light"?
Did Sir Phidipaldi take Sir Brandon's holy sword and strip the plate armor from his remains?
Did Sir Phidipaldi give his own plate armor to his day laborer and don Sir Brandon's plate armor?
As the party prepared to leave Sir Brandon's burial chamber, did a seven-foot brown skeleton in rusted armor and a mustachioed death mask appear in the doorway, dragging a huge greatsword?
Does Drop Dead Ned carry a killer wasp in a jar?
Did the barrow's entrance bear a faded mural depicting a conquering knight?
Did the barrow's entrance  bear mosaics portraying Myrddin as a wizened priest and Wyllt as a wild-eyed axeman among Sir Brandon's companions?
Did a mosaic depict Sir Brandon being honored alongside his surviving company after the dragon's death?
Did Grimble Who Holds the Stick tell Sir Phidipaldi that the Free Goblin Society recognized neither titles nor hereditary property and had fled a king to put no person above another?
Did Watok the Scribbler say that the party could either give goods to every goblin or pay nothing, since the collective rejected property?
Did an alcove in the goblin crypt contain dusty bones, a chain shirt, and a mace?
Did Squints collect some of the dead ooze in his pocket to show people back home?
Did Drop Dead Ned produce a crowbar so Waymon Tisdale could pry open a concealed panel?
